principles.text: Treat your recent trade feedback as a market signal: when solid, well-selected setups keep getting stopped out, the market itself is telling you to cut exposure and reassess your posture.
Judge a group by its leader: in a strong uptrend the leader must bounce hard off the 9 EMA. A failed 9 EMA bounce that drifts sideways near the low of day is an early warning to sell the whole group.
Parabolic/climactic dollar-volume after a huge extended run (e.g. consecutive ~$100B volume days after a near-1000% move) often marks the swing high or the end of the uptrend.
When volatility expands after a long rally (big gaps up and down, wide candles, failed breakouts), it generally means distribution or consolidation, not continuation.

Individual names showing relative weakness before the sector breaks (losing the 9/21 EMA, 9 crossing below 21, repeated failed breakouts, first close below the 50 EMA) flag the coming turn and become the pullback-short candidates.
Avoid trading the first 15-30 minutes after open. If the sector ETF gaps down and you want to short, wait for the bounce instead of chasing the open.
Once a breakdown has already extended, it is too late to short. Wait for the rebound into the declining 9/21 EMA (or the anchored VWAP from the swing high) for the short entry.
In a weak group's bounce, short the names that get rejected at the 9 EMA while retesting prior base/swing lows -- a breakdown-and-retest trend-continuation setup.
Skip groups that are acting well but moving too slowly -- only trade the fast movers.
Scale out by selling into strength rather than dumping the entire position at once into weakness.
When the action feels weird, strange, or uncomfortable midday, act on it -- take positions off rather than staying stubborn or long-biased.
Losses are a chain reaction: early sloppy losses consume your risk budget and force you to pass on the day's best setup later. Protecting the open preserves capacity for the A+ trade.
Do not get aggressively bearish inside a potential chop zone. Require confirmation -- e.g. the index closing below the 9 and 21 EMA -- before increasing short exposure.
Use holidays and long weekends to digest the action across names, review your trades, and fix mistakes so you come back with a refreshed mind.
